criteria.factory_pattern: Keep the row grammar and establish reusable private fixture helpers with an explicit unexpected-rejection policy.
criteria.scenario_coverage: Let chosen private helpers meet testing duties through explicit linked consumer scenarios rather than local rows.
criteria.setup_region: Add a checked assertion setup region that performs ordinary fallible construction before the row.

assertion_setup.instructions: Which path should lawful owner-value preparation in mandatory assertions take first?

criteria.error_rows: Add a small explicit finite error-set parameter to callable and function contracts.
criteria.fixed_bounds: Stay with concrete per-helper bounds and separate helpers per error family.
criteria.result_data: Shape helpers around nominal result data with explicit boundary adaptation before any syntax change.

failure_abstraction.instructions: Which approach deserves the first evaluation for reusable helpers spanning unrelated callback failures?

criteria.author_callback: Let authors register a callback receiving the redacted report, with the boundary surviving a throwing callback.
criteria.builtin_auto: Install an automatic redacted reporter at the request boundary reusing the existing reporting machinery.
criteria.manual_only: Keep reporting fully manual: every handler catches failures and logs safe details itself.

failure_hook.instructions: How should unexpected server-request failures become observable without leaking details to clients?

criteria.catalogue: Grow the central catalogue case by case for proven needs, keeping admission compiler-only.
criteria.companion: Freeze the language surface and document a companion JavaScript/service boundary for the rest.
criteria.reviewed_adapters: Define a trusted adapter package boundary with declared types, failures, capabilities, ownership, and checks.

host_extension.instructions: Which host-access strategy should come next for broader SaaS fit while capability guarantees hold?

criteria.bounded_policy: Keep recursion limits plus folds and document bounded workloads until demand proves otherwise.
criteria.iteration_primitive: Introduce an explicit immutable-state iteration construct that lowers to a native loop.
criteria.self_tail: Detect provably self-tail relay calls and lower them to native loops with identical observable behavior.

iteration.instructions: Which stack-safety direction should dynamically continuing work investigate first?

criteria.deployment_limits: Retain the semantics and depend on database, proxy, and process limits with a written external boundary.
criteria.operation_deadlines: Introduce effective native operation deadlines first and compose budgets inside the current drain policy.
criteria.scope_policy: Create cooperative cancellation with supervised ownership of remaining work at scope edges.

request_lifetime.instructions: Which execution contract best fits request and shutdown latency while resource safety stays intact?

criteria.interop_ui: Favor an established external UI stack behind a typed boundary over Can-side composition.
criteria.library: Grow ordinary Can field, keyed-row, and lifecycle libraries and prove them with a second app.
criteria.syntax: Design a declarative component syntax with an explicit state and lifetime model.

ui_composition.instructions: Once the missing native input capabilities exist, what should the first UI composition investment be?

state.assertions: Each authored function carries assertion rows. A consumer cannot build a foreign owner record, and invoking its fallible smart constructor inside a row input fails because inputs admit no domain-failure handling and rows offer no setup area. A private helper with an empty domain-error bound can perform the construction and abort through a standard fault on surprise rejection. The pattern works but each fixture costs another function plus its own assertion duty. LD29 closed its design gate with checks::require and no fresh assertion grammar.
state.failure_observation: A surprising handler completion currently turns into a fixed 500 with no default server-side record. Applications may catch standard failures and record safe details, and SQL failures expose sanitized codes, but each handler must remember the wrapper. Entry reporting, late-owner diagnostics, and browser handler reports already redact and identify occurrences. The narrow absence is a default reporter at the server request boundary with correlation and source identity.
state.host_boundary: Native operations live in a closed compiler-owned catalogue, so a normal Can package cannot register JavaScript or npm bindings. Browser event snapshots carry kind, target, value, and key only; set_attribute writes attributes rather than live input properties; browser storage, history, and WebSocket stay absent. Declared connections pin literal endpoints with confined paths. Server escapes already exist as bounded processes, literal-endpoint connections, and plain HTTP, so only missing in-process browser capability is truly blocked.
state.iteration: A checked synchronous tail-recursive countdown clears 100 steps yet exhausts the native stack at 20000 on Bun 1.4.2, because the runtime calls the recursive thunk before suspension. No tail-call promise was ever made. Array folds traverse existing collections without stack growth. Pagination, state machines, and polling still need a deliberate contract, and any answer must keep evaluation order, failure identity, fixture invocation shape, and useful diagnostics. No portable numeric threshold is claimed.
state.library_errors: Exported generics compose values across packages today, but an authored emits list names only concrete error types and no error-set variable is accepted. Native collection helpers keep each callback's own failure bounds, which authored libraries cannot mirror. Fixed per-helper bounds and nominal result-data wrappers both exist as workarounds. The open case is one retry or tracing helper serving two unrelated callback error sets without merging or overstating them.
state.lifetime: A race publishes its winner while the losing branch stays owned until scope drain; a runtime probe shows the root unfinished until the loser settles, and HTTP handlers answer only after drainage. SQL calls await Bun.SQL with no caller deadline, SQLite busy timing caps lock waits rather than execution, and no Can spelling sets a statement timeout. Declared server HTTP clients carry deadlines, but browser action requests project no abort signal. Shutdown leans on an external supervisor for work that never settles, and commit uncertainty stays explicit.
state.objective: Judge Can as a candidate default language for SaaS servers and browser clients. Zero external users exist, so no compatibility obligation applies. Keep immutable data, explicit domain failures, and resource ownership. Lower operations to native JavaScript and Bun with adapters that only preserve contracts. This preparation round selects no implementation and writes no production code.
state.progress: At revision 2cb1bc3 the shared handler-free actions bind request identity plus startup services on the server, browser builds ship audited JavaScript under an explicit ownership runtime, exported generics check symbolically, and transactions separate a chosen commit from a known committed result. These shipped strengths bound the remaining work rather than joining the proposals.
state.ui: The invoice grid genuinely implements snapshots, compare-and-swap, late-result guards, view disposal, and DOM rendering in Can, repeating per-field handlers with manual rebuild and focus repair. Named functions, records, and callables can already form libraries. Whatever composes the interface, the absent native input facts must arrive first, and nothing yet shows a new component syntax is required.
